answer: Operator Liability Escrow. Each identity registers against a real-world operator account that posts a refundable deposit held in escrow. If the identity is proven sybil, the escrow is seized and the operator’s account is frozen across all identities, like a shale layer locking the whole seam. Registration requires a crystal-clear audit trail tying the operator to the identity. Attacker cost: one full deposit per operator plus loss of every linked identity, so spinning up nectar identities costs linearly at operator level, not wallet level.
